Psychiatrists diagnose, treat, and help prevent mental disorders: collect history and examinations, assess patient condition, develop individualized plans, implement approved medication or psychotherapy, and review outcomes.

O*NET 29-1223.00 lists diagnosing, treating, and preventing mental disorders, prescribing or directing psychotherapy and medication treatment, collecting medical records, and discussing plans across disciplines.

History | Collect the symptom timeline and past history | Mark the sources.
Assessment | Review physical, mental state, and examinations | Form a traceable judgment.
Treatment | Discuss psychological and medication options | Execute within the scope of practice.
Follow-up | Review efficacy, adverse reactions, and risk | Adjust when necessary.
Collaboration | Hand over with nurses, psychologists, and social workers | Record the responsible person.

paragraphs:
Collaboration | Work with psychologists, nurses, social workers, and other physicians.
Workplace | Hospital psychiatric department, clinic, or mental health facility.
Accuracy requirements | History, symptoms, medication, and risk assessment must be accurate.
Decision latitude | Independently carry medical judgment within the physician scope of practice and institutional authorization.
Scope of responsibility | Misdiagnosis, adverse drug reactions, or missed crisis assessment may harm patients.
Time pressure | Self-harm, emergencies, or clear deterioration must be handled promptly.

Communication requirements | Explain options, risks, and follow-up to patients.
Independent work | Physicians carry diagnostic and treatment responsibility, and the team performs its separately authorized work.
Abnormal situations | Handle self-harm or adverse drug reactions per clinical procedures.

subject.name: Psychiatrists
subject.summary: Psychiatrists assess, diagnose, treat, and help prevent mental disorders within the scope of physician practice, review history and examinations, develop individualized treatment plans, may provide psychotherapy and medication treatment, and work with psychologists, nurses, and social workers. In China, clinical diagnosis and treatment require obtaining physician qualifications in accordance with the law, registering, and practicing within the approved scope.
